metadata.title: Packet Walkthrough and Worked Examples
metadata.subject: NCC — Net-Centric Computing
metadata.contentType: Original practice based on the accompanying lecture notes

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.sentence: A greeting starting at sequence 7001 with 39 bytes is acknowledged by ___.
questions.explanation: TCP ACK reports the next expected byte.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.sentence: The exact EHLO command in the packet example contains ___ payload bytes including CRLF.
hints: 24 printable bytes and two control bytes.
questions.explanation: The line terminator contributes two bytes to the TCP stream.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.sentence: With 20-byte IP and TCP headers and 26 payload bytes, IPv4 Total Length is ___.
questions.explanation: Ethernet framing is outside IPv4 Total Length.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.sentence: The resulting untagged Ethernet MAC frame including FCS is ___ bytes.
hints: Add 18 bytes to the IP packet.
questions.explanation: No Ethernet padding is needed for a 66-byte payload.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: For a 1500-byte MTU and option-free IPv4 and TCP, the TCP payload limit is ___ bytes.
questions.explanation: The headers consume 40 bytes of the IP packet budget.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: A 5000-byte stream split into three 1460-byte payloads has a final payload of ___ bytes.
questions.explanation: Payload totals must equal the application byte count.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: At 100 Mb/s, serializing 12000 bits takes ___ microseconds.
hints: Bits divided by bits per second.
questions.explanation: The result excludes link framing overhead.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: A 2000 km path at 2 × 10^8 m/s has a propagation delay of ___ ms.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: Seven round trips of 40 ms total ___ ms in the stated timing example.
questions.explanation: Different TLS, pipelining, cache, and greeting assumptions change the model.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.sentence: Base64 encodes 3000 input bytes into ___ characters before wrapping.
questions.explanation: Line endings, MIME boundaries, and part headers add more bytes.

questions.sentence: The receiving SMTP process reads reconstructed TCP ___ rather than directly reading Ethernet frames.
questions.explanation: TCP supplies contiguous stream bytes through the socket.

source.section: Section 15 — Failure analysis and explained cases

questions.sentence: The final SMTP acceptance reply after content is commonly ___, whereas a TCP ACK proves only transport receipt.
hints: Three-digit success code used in the dialogue.
questions.explanation: Acceptance by one server still does not prove reading by the recipient.
